proposals.before: In those days Xiao Yu, son of General Wang, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Wan, were celebrated heirs of the elite, and Zhu Bo numbered among their companions.
proposals.after: In those days Xiao Yu, son of Former General Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Wannian, were celebrated heirs of the elite, and Zhu Bo numbered among their companions.
proposals.reason: Chinese 前將軍望之 names Former General Wangzhi, not 'General Wang'; 御史大夫萬年 names Wannian, not 'Wan'.

proposals.before: At that time Xiao Yu, son of the former general Wang, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Wan, were famous as sons of dukes and ministers of outstanding talent; Bo was already friends with them.
proposals.after: At that time Xiao Yu, son of the former general Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Wannian, were famous as sons of dukes and ministers of outstanding talent; Bo was already friends with them.
proposals.reason: Same as idiomatic: 望之 and 萬年 are the fathers' personal names, not truncated 'Wang' and 'Wan'.

proposals.before: The emperor recalled Xue Xuan, restored his title as Marquis of Gaoyang, advanced him to specially advanced rank just below Tutor Shi of Anchang, gave him a palace attendant post, and assigned him to oversee secretariat business.
proposals.after: The emperor recalled Xue Xuan, restored his title as Marquis of Gaoyang, advanced him to specially advanced rank just below the Tutor Marquis of Anchang, gave him a palace attendant post, and assigned him to oversee secretariat business.
proposals.reason: In 師安昌侯, 師 is the office 'tutor', not a surname Shi.

proposals.before: Four years on, Ai renamed the chancellor grand tutor and reinstated grand minister of works and grand marshal.
proposals.after: Four years on, Ai renamed the chancellor grand minister of education and reinstated grand minister of works and grand marshal.
proposals.reason: 大司徒 is the grand minister of education (grand situ), not the grand tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: Four years later Emperor Ai changed the chancellor to grand tutor, and again set grand minister of works and grand marshal.
proposals.after: Four years later Emperor Ai changed the chancellor to grand minister of education, and again set grand minister of works and grand marshal.
proposals.reason: 大司徒 should not be rendered as grand tutor; that office is 太傅.

proposals.before: General of the Right Wang Jiao and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
proposals.after: General of the Right Jiao Wang and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
proposals.reason: Chinese 蟜望 is surname 蟜 plus given name 望; English Wang Jiao reverses the name order and wrong surname reading.

proposals.before: General of the Right Wang Jiao and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
proposals.after: General of the Right Jiao Wang and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
proposals.reason: 蟜望 should be Jiao Wang, not Wang Jiao.

proposals.before: when Sun Qiaoru of Lu slandered his kinsman Ji Xingfu to Jin and threw Lu into chaos, the Annals condemned it harshly.
proposals.after: when Shusun Qiaoru of Lu wished to monopolize the ducal house and slandered his agnate elder Jisun Xingfu to Jin, and Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, throwing Lu into chaos, the Annals condemned it harshly.
proposals.reason: 叔孫僑如 is Shusun Qiaoru, not Sun Qiaoru; the idiomatic line also omits his aim to monopolize the ducal house.

proposals.before: Lu grandee Sun Qiaoru wished to monopolize the ducal house and slandered his agnate elder Xingfu to Jin; Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, disordering Lu—the Spring and Autumn thought it weighty and recorded it.
proposals.after: Lu grandee Shusun Qiaoru wished to monopolize the ducal house and slandered his agnate elder Xingfu to Jin; Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, disordering Lu—the Spring and Autumn thought it weighty and recorded it.
proposals.reason: Literal drops 叔 from 叔孫, yielding Sun Qiaoru instead of Shusun Qiaoru.

decisions.after: In those days Xiao Yu, son of Former General Xiao Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Chen Wannian, were celebrated heirs of the elite, and Zhu Bo numbered among their companions.
decisions.reason: 望之 and 萬年 are Xiao Wangzhi and Chen Wannian. The proposal restores their given names but still omits both surnames.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前將軍望之子蕭育，御史大夫萬年子陳咸

decisions.after: At that time Xiao Yu, son of former general Xiao Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Chen Wannian, were famous as talented sons of dukes and ministers; Zhu Bo was already friends with them.
decisions.reason: The fathers are Xiao Wangzhi and Chen Wannian. Restoring only Wangzhi and Wannian would leave both full names incomplete.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前將軍望之…御史大夫萬年

decisions.after: The emperor recalled Xue Xuan, restored his title as Marquis of Gaoyang, advanced him to specially advanced rank just below his tutor, Zhang Yu, Marquis of Anchang, gave him a palace attendant post, and assigned him to oversee secretariat business.
decisions.reason: 師 identifies the emperor's tutor, Zhang Yu, Marquis of Anchang, rather than a man surnamed Shi. The proposal's 'Tutor Marquis' is still awkward and obscures the construction.
改丞相為大司徒 renames the chancellorship to grand minister of education (situ); grand tutor would be 太傅.
大司徒 is grand minister of education, not grand tutor; the literal repair correctly distinguishes it from 太傅.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 改丞相為大司徒，復置大司空、大司馬焉

decisions.reason: 蟜望 is surname 蟜 plus given name 望, so Jiao Wang; Wang Jiao reverses the name and misreads the surname.
Same naming error in the literal: 蟜望 must be Jiao Wang, not Wang Jiao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 右將軍蟜望等四十四人

decisions.after: when Shusun Qiaoru of Lu tried to monopolize the ducal house by slandering his clan elder Jisun Xingfu to Jin, and Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, thereby throwing Lu into disorder, the Annals treated the affair as grave enough to record.
decisions.reason: The proposal restores both compound surnames and the omitted events, but 重而書之 means the Annals treated the affair as grave enough to record, not simply that they condemned it harshly.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魯大夫叔孫僑如欲顓公室，譖其族兄季孫行父於晉，晉執囚行父以亂魯國

decisions.after: The Lu grandee Shusun Qiaoru wished to monopolize the ducal house and slandered his clan elder Jisun Xingfu to Jin; Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, throwing Lu into disorder, and the Spring and Autumn Annals treated the affair as grave enough to record.
decisions.reason: 叔孫 and 季孫 are the compound surnames Shusun and Jisun. The proposal fixes only Shusun and leaves Jisun omitted, while 重而書之 also needs an accurate subject and sense.

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted repair shows the English personal name Wang Jiao was an inverted misreading of 蟜望; the correct English is Jiao Wang.
The accepted repair restores the compound surname 叔孫; English Sun Qiaoru was produced by the truncated translation.
The accepted repair restores 季孫 as Jisun; English Ji Xingfu truncated the clan surname from the bad idiomatic rendering.
